Uncommon Thinkers: Andrew Redd’s audacious plan to turn ocean volcanoes into power plants

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1244 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 24, 2026 at 9:53 am.
  • In a recent development, editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec.
  • Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 24, 2026 at 9:53 am.

In a recent development, editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec. 10 at the GeekWire Gala in partnership with Greater Seattle Partners.

Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.

The dots connect, but the picture they form is anything but ordinary: bold in vision, fast in execution and enormous in potential.

Redd has next-level ambition, and he’s directing it at solving one of the world’s biggest and most urgent problems — adding renewable, massively scalable energy that can outcompete fossil fuels and reach the grid quickly enough to make a difference in the race against climate change.

Industry observers note that underwater geothermal energy has never been tapped in a significant way, but to Redd, the idea was irresistible. “It checks all of the boxes for our perfect future energy source,” he remarked.

In a recent development, he founded Endurance Energy on the north shore of Seattle’s Lake Union in January 2025, and this September the team oversaw its fifth deep-sea deployment. At a site 300 miles off the Oregon coast, its prototype system generated more electricity than it consumed. The startup has raised $63 million from investors and has roughly three dozen employees.

Recent findings suggest that nate Bek, a principal at Ascend, praised Redd’s ability to attract “brilliant” talent in pursuit of his goal. The Seattle venture firm is one of the startup’s early backers.

“I’ve been deeply inspired by what [Redd]’s building at Endurance and haven’t shut up about it since the day we met,” Bek noted. “He somehow makes powering the world from the bottom of the ocean feel inevitable, all while remaining remarkably measured and transparent about the progress.”.

According to recent reports, for Redd, studying engineering and aerospace in college was so clear-cut that it wasn’t a choice at all. Growing up around Boeing, seaplanes, the Museum of Flight and the Pacific Northwest’s rich maritime industry naturally pointed him toward those sectors. He wanted a degree as expansive as his influences.

It has been revealed that “I didn’t really want to have to choose whether it was going to be boats or space travel or airplanes,” he said. “I just wanted to be able to do anything — keep the world as wide open as possible.”.

After graduating from Princeton University, Redd worked at Neuralink, an Elon Musk company developing technology that lets the brain communicate directly with computers. A year later, in 2021, he moved to Musk’s rocket company, SpaceX.

That was another no-duh decision, as Redd viewed it.

“I saw SpaceX as really the place to be, where early-career people are given the most amount of resources and responsibility, and that felt like the fastest way to learn and the most engaging possible scenario to be in,” Redd said. “I wanted to be tossed into something that was a little bit crazy.”.

In a recent development, redd joined as SpaceX was starting to build its first orbital Starship rockets. The program brought together passionate young people and experienced SpaceX engineers who served as mentors. Wild ideas were entertained and explored. Everyone was committed to the mission. It was just the experience Redd wanted, and he planned to stick around for seven to 10 years.

Then artificial intelligence started booming.

In 2024, the build-out of sprawling, energy-hungry data centers for AI was accelerating with no end in sight. At the same time, efforts to electrify transportation, heating and cooling were driving up demand for power. Redd saw these trends sparking a surge in upcoming natural gas generation, locking in decades of carbon emissions.

It has been revealed that he wanted to find a better way. He went into engineering mode, focusing on all the essential criteria for an energy source: it had to be clean, not dependent on intermittent sun or wind, capable of producing massive amounts of energy, readily deployable, subject to fewer regulatory hurdles than something like nuclear, economically competitive, and scalable.

Redd recognized the tremendous heat contained under Earth’s surface as a terrific source for renewable energy and realized that most of the world’s active volcanoes are offshore. The unknown was whether the rocky ocean floor would be suitable for geothermal wells, so he did some research and found publications from geology experts who said the conditions would be “perfect.”.

“You can tell,” he said, “when there’s a moment in time that you need to go and reach out and grab something, and that was really my impression — if I didn’t start this now, this would never come into existence, or wouldn’t come into existence soon enough to make a meaningful impact.”.

In a recent development, in launching Endurance, Redd was intentional about the culture he wanted to create. He was aiming for a multidisciplinary group of mission-driven employees eager to collaborate and learn from each other: top talent that would attract more of the same and make Endurance a place people were excited to work.

“The hardest part of an early-stage startup is recruiting,” Redd noted, “especially if you’re a first-time founder.”.

The startup employs about a dozen SpaceX alumni, plus employees from the fusion organization Helion Energy and the aerospace venture Blue Origin.

It has been revealed that A strong team is key to Endurance’s success. That’s because, enthusiasm and passion aside, the startup faces steep engineering and economic challenges. The technology must withstand high pressure, corrosive conditions and mineral scaling inside devices, and seafloor machinery could be costly to repair. The systems will need expensive subsea cables to carry power to shore over potentially long distances. It’s a heavy lift.

While the September sea trial didn’t go perfectly, Redd is happy with the results. The company landed its 3-ton power plant on the seafloor near a natural vent and produced net energy from it — albeit for only 8.7 seconds. Technical difficulties and a power-cable failure cut the dive short.

In a recent development, team members successfully operated the system remotely from Seattle through a fiber-optic network running along the seabed. Redd mentioned he’s grateful for access to the network, which is part of the National Science Foundation’s Regional Cabled Array and operated by the University of Washington.

Endurance engineers also drilled what they called the world’s first subsea geothermal well at a site about 5,000 feet below the ocean’s surface. The 2-inch-wide, 52-foot-deep well delivered hydrothermal fluid, but the flow was too restricted to run the power plant, sending the team to the natural vent.

Redd said there’s a lot of work ahead, but the team “made huge strides” in learning and in reducing the project’s risks.

Recent findings suggest that the organization now is developing Leopard, its 2-megawatt generator. After testing the technology at the research site off the Oregon coast, Endurance aims to deliver power from a Leopard system in Tonga next year as its first commercial project. Subsea geothermal energy could ultimately reduce the island nation’s reliance on imported diesel and put the startup one step closer to its objective of generating terawatts of planet-friendly energy.

“This was always the end goal,” Redd remarked. “Create something that is highly meaningful for the world.”.

Editor’s Note: Nate Bek of Ascend is a former GeekWire reporter.

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, has recorded a multi-month high in daily trading volume as the cryptocurrency market remains in the grip of extreme volatility.

Recent findings suggest that the massive spike in trading volume comes after Bitcoin tanked to two-year lows on Nov. 21 before bouncing back sharply to regain ground toward the psychologically crucial $60,000 level.

The massive spike in trading volume comes in the wake of one of the biggest sell-offs in BTC this year.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 21, the world’s largest cryptocurrency dropped as low as around $55,100, a level last seen in September 2024. The sharp decline in Bitcoin prices came as risk assets tumbled amid rising concerns over the U.S. stock market and the artificial intelligence (AI) sector, which weighed on investor sentiment.

Following the sharp plunge, Bitcoin managed to make a stunning comeback as the flagship cryptocurrency recovered to trade back above $60,000 and briefly pushed toward the $61,000 mark.

The comeback, however, was short-lived as BTC lost ground again and tanked below the crucial $60,000 mark.

BTC is right now trading at around $58,879, rising 5.4% in the last 24 hours, as per the latest data from CoinGecko.

Furthermore, the world’s largest cryptocurrency has a 24-hour trading volume of around $43.8 billion and has regained a market cap of $1.18 trillion.

Recent findings suggest that as per data from analytics firm CoinGlass, Bitcoin (BTC) futures trading volume stands at around $76.17 billion. On the other hand, the cryptocurrency's spot trading volume stands at $7.91 billion over the past 24 hours.

Despite the latest recovery, it is still trading 9.74% lower over the past seven days and more than 27% lower over the past month.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency is also down around 53.3% from its all-time high of $126,198.

Another massive wave of liquidations has swept through the cryptocurrency market following the latest recovery.

As per the latest data from CoinGlass, 85,533 traders have been liquidated in the last 24 hours, with total liquidations amounting to $562.12 million.

It is worth noting that around $406.13 million in liquidations were on the short side, while only $156 million were on the long side.

With regard to BTC, it alone accounts for around $346.18 million in liquidations, and a staggering 76.7% of those liquidations were on the bearish side.

At the moment, Bitcoin is unable to reclaim the $60,000 level with conviction.

#146104. Breaking: How real estate agents handle proof of funds and disclosures

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1175 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: How real estate agents handle proof of funds and disclosures

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1175 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On a recent coaching call this week, an agent asked a question that looks tactical and is actually about professional discipline.
  • Let me give the coaching first, because the sequence is where most agents go wrong.
  • Proof of funds gets requested too early and in the wrong tone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On a recent coaching call this week, an agent asked a question that looks tactical and is actually about professional discipline. She works mostly in commercial, she has a physician buying a home and several of her clients have investors behind them, which makes gathering proof of funds a real ordeal. When do I ask for it? Does it need to be current? And how do I protect something that private? Those questions sit squarely on the line between being a salesperson and being a fiduciary, and that line is where our industry keeps getting tested.

Let me give the coaching first, because the sequence is where most agents go wrong.

Proof of funds gets requested too early and in the wrong tone. Imagine a buyer who just called on an ad. If the first thing you do is hand them a list of documents, you have converted a warm first contact into homework, and you have done it before you have given them a single reason to trust you. I do not open any client relationship by burdening the person with tasks. The order has to serve the relationship, not the file.

Here is the sequence I teach. Get them into the office first. On that opening call you can ask one soft question, do you happen to have a proof of funds ready, and if the answer is no, you keep it light. We will need it at some point, bring it when we meet if you can, but do not worry about it now. You have raised the flag without turning it into a barrier.

Industry observers note that when they arrive, run a genuine buyer appointment and get the buyer to hire you, the same way you would work to get hired by a seller. Only then do you assign the homework, and now the identical list that would have felt like a wall on the phone lands as a blueprint. Here is what we need from you, and in the meantime let’s define exactly what you are looking for, let me show you what is available, and we can even see a couple so you get a feel for the market. The serious looking begins once I have the documents. The buyer never feels interrogated. They feel represented.

Powerfact: You earn the right to ask for documents by first earning the relationship.

Now to the part that matters for leaders, because it is about how we protect our businesses and our clients at the same time.

In a recent development, she asked whether to send buyers to their own bank or recommend someone she knows. I prefer to recommend my own lender, and I say that carefully, because we are operating in a litigation environment, and the professional move is to assume you could be sued and to run your business so that you are covered. Practically, that means disclosing any financial relationship in writing, every time. On our coaching platform I built a document I call the Transparency Conversation, a simple editable form that states who you are connected to, how you get paid, and whether anyone shares in a fee. If the lender is tied to your organization and a financial arrangement exists, that gets disclosed plainly. If you are recommending someone purely because you know and trust the loan officer, you say exactly that and nothing more.

Here is how I used to present the recommendation itself, and the logic has aged well. You can use any lender you want, that is your call. The reason I like my person is this. I could refer a lot of lenders, and I choose this one, because if he ever lets you down, he does not just lose your loan, he loses every piece of business I will ever send him. So he will do whatever it takes, within the rules, to get you to the closing table. That framing respects the buyer’s freedom and explains why your recommendation carries weight. It is service, stated out loud.

Her question was about confidentiality. She had a buyer with roughly $2 million in proof of funds, and people are private about money at that level. Does it become confidential? Do we keep the figure quiet even though we hold the documentation?

This is where the fiduciary line gets drawn. The moment a buyer hires you, they stop being a customer and become a client, and that shift carries a duty. Anything they share with you stays with you unless they authorize otherwise. So think like an attorney. When the information is this sensitive, you protect it with a document. Have the client sign an authorization that permits you to share their financial information only with the parties who truly need it to assemble the transaction. You can adapt the Transparency Conversation form for exactly this. Now you can do your job, the client’s privacy is respected, and you have a record that protects both of you.

Sources indicate that another agent said she never provides proof of funds until after an offer is accepted. That is a sound default in many cases, but it depends on the seller. On luxury homes, estates, and commercial property, the listing side will often require proof of funds before they open the door, and that is legitimate. Sellers of a multimillion dollar property do not want a stream of non-buyers touring for decorating ideas or dream-board photos. When you represent that buyer, prepare them for the requirement so a reasonable request does not feel like an insult.

In a recent development, for brokers and team leaders, here is the translation. Our industry has spent two years being told that our compensation and our value must be disclosed, documented, and justified. Good. The agents who will thrive under that scrutiny are the ones who already behave like fiduciaries by habit, not the ones who treat disclosure as a form to dodge. Teach your people the sequence, relationship first, documents second. Standardize the written disclosures so no agent is improvising a legal boundary on the fly. And model the confidentiality, because a buyer who sees you guard their two million dollar statement like it is your own will refer you for the rest of their life.

According to recent reports, the whole thing fits on one page. Do not lead with the paperwork. Get them in, get them to hire you, assign the homework as part of the service. Recommend your lender, and disclose everything in writing. Treat their financial information as a fiduciary, with a signed authorization. And read the other side of the transaction, so you know when a request for proof is simply professionalism doing its job.

Darryl Davis, CSP, is a national speaker, real estate coach, and the bestselling author of How to Become a Power Agent® in Real Estate. Learn more at darrylspeaks.com.

So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1404 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.
  • Sources indicate that nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn.
  • Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a big decision to make in the next few weeks: take the company’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.

Sources indicate that nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Massive Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a big decision to make in the next few weeks: take the company’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The organization expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

According to recent reports, microsoft indicates the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

Recent findings suggest that the offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in fresh hires.

The worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the manufacturer decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a tech giant right now?

Harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

There is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

One of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

But it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one company.

Hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more key than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

The jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

Recent findings suggest that AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI firm today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Recent findings suggest that hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual organization. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software company.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a company.

Software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

This cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the big platforms will copy anything that works.

It has been revealed that the true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue rapidly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

The bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

It has been revealed that one venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

There are three fundraising paths.

Industry observers note that 1) Think VERY big, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

Industry observers note that 2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a manufacturer that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

In a recent development, there are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

In a recent development, other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

Recent findings suggest that whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Substantial Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a new role, a manufacturer of their own or a year with their family.

#146101. What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1550 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

What music sells a house? Agents say it’s not about genre

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that taylor Swift, classical or silence?
  • According to recent reports, ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers.
  • Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that taylor Swift, classical or silence? Agents explain how they pick open house music, the one rule most follow and why none can prove it works.

According to recent reports, ask real estate agents what soundtrack sells a house, and you’ll get two answers. One is a carefully curated playlist, while the other is silence.

Inman asked agents and brokers from Manhattan to Breckenridge, Colorado, and they described the music they play at showings and open houses and how they match it to the property.

It has been revealed that none could point to hard numbers showing a playlist moved a home faster or for more money. What they did offer was a clear set of rules from the agents who use music, and an equally firm argument from those who won’t touch it.

Ben Jacobs, co-founder of the Chestler Jacobs Team at Douglas Elliman in New York City, thinks music raises more questions than it answers. He stated he’s not a fan of playing music during showings.

According to recent reports, “Buyers may wonder if the agent is trying to mask something, whether it’s street noise, construction nearby, sounds within the building or even a noisy appliance,” Jacobs told Inman. “You want buyers to experience the home as it actually is, without anything distracting from their ability to evaluate the space.”.

His co-founder, Jessica Chestler, said music has its place. That place is just not a private showing.

“Music can be wonderful for setting a mood at a cocktail party, listing launch or special event, but during a showing, I think there’s something to be said for letting the property speak for itself,” Chestler said.

Megan Sullivan works at the same brokerage, and she uses music for the very reason Jacobs avoids it. Sullivan sells large estate homes across Fairfield and Westchester counties out of Douglas Elliman’s Greenwich, Connecticut, office. Some of those homes sit within earshot of things a seller can’t fix.

Industry observers note that “I actually do like incorporating music into certain showings, particularly when a property is impacted by outside noise from planes, trains or automobiles,” Sullivan said. “Thoughtfully selected background music can help create a more welcoming atmosphere and soften those distractions, allowing buyers to focus on the overall experience of the home. I think it’s very property-specific.”.

According to recent reports, jeffrey Hensel is a broker associate with North Coast Financial, a California hard money lender that funds fix-and-flip and probate deals. He looks at it from the investor side.

“Dead silence can amplify every creak, clank, and drip in an otherwise quiet home,” he said. “Background music masks these sounds and provides some white noise to help set a calm mood.”.

It has been revealed that agents in the pro-music camp mostly aren’t trying to cover anything up. They simply want buyers to stay longer.

It has been revealed that sandra Daniels of Harry Norman, Realtors | Forbes Global Properties serves the East Cobb and Marietta area outside Atlanta. She’s currently listing a $3.9 million estate in The River Club in Suwanee, Georgia.

For those showings, she rotates light classical piano, The Macarons Project and a Spotify playlist called “Nora Ephron + Nancy Meyers Dinner Party.”.

“Put a buyer in a home with a glass of Champagne or a cup of coffee and the right music playing, and that cozy, inviting atmosphere encourages people to stay, relax and feel at home,” Daniels told Inman.

Daniels also has a low-tech trick for vacant listings she expects to sell in the first week. She bought an old-school CD player and a few classical CDs. She leaves it on repeat through the first weekend of showings and stops by each evening to turn off the lights and music and lock up.

Natalia Bassova, founder and CEO of Resort Real Estate in Breckenridge, Colorado, saw the same effect at a luxury mountain listing. The home looked great, she noted, but it indicated cold.

In a recent development, “By adding some background instrumental music, it gave the buyers more time to spend in the home. They spent more time in the kitchen and great room areas,” Bassova mentioned. “The property didn’t change, but the atmosphere did.”.

It has been revealed that for mountain and luxury homes, Bassova plays acoustic and piano music, including Ludovico Einaudi and The Piano Guys. For condos and newly introduced construction, she switches to soft contemporary instrumentals.

Agents who play music disagree on genre, but almost all agree on one thing: avoid lyrics.

Sources indicate that “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact,” Bassova said. Her never-play list covers anything with strong lyrics, politics, swearing or heavy bass.

Sources indicate that andrea Seeney is a global real estate advisor with Atlanta Fine Homes Sotheby’s International Realty and a trained opera singer and classical pianist. She compared lyrics to a seller’s personal effects.

“Acoustic performances are best because they set a tone and allow the buyer to fill in the blanks with their own thoughts,” Seeney remarked.

She leans toward jazz and usually plays Spotify’s Coffee House radio or its Ella Fitzgerald playlist. She says music works on buyers through memory: a song can take someone back to a time and place they enjoyed, “and that memory then reflects positively on the home.”.

According to recent reports, hensel takes the lyrics rule a step further, to genre itself. If an agent plays hip-hop or country for a buyer who doesn’t listen to it, he says, that signals an assumption about who the buyer is. That can create friction neither side notices. His pick is quiet cocktail-lounge jazz like Miles Davis or Bill Evans, at a steady tempo and volume.

According to recent reports, he also cited retail research by psychological scientists Adrian North and Lorraine Sheridan of Curtin University and Charles Areni of Macquarie University. It found that shoppers who heard classical music rated merchandise as higher quality and were willing to spend more.

Some agents ignore the rulebook completely.

Recent findings suggest that rachel Kilmer, an agent with ReeceNichols Real Estate in Kansas City, Missouri, plays Taylor Swift at nearly every open house. She swaps in country for more rural listings.

“In Kansas City, she’s a conversation starter,” Kilmer stated. “People come in, and it’s, ‘Are you a Swiftie?’ ‘No, but I love the Chiefs!’ It really helps loosen up the conversation.”.

She added, “I’m the one sitting there listening to it for two hours!”.

Monica Shea, a broker with KW Aspire in Colorado Springs, Colorado, builds whole open houses around a theme, and the music follows.

Sources indicate that she played the Eras Tour set list at a Taylor Swift–themed open house and the Frozen soundtrack at a hot cocoa bar event. A Halloween open house got not-too-spooky Halloween music. For regular showings, she has sellers put on a YouTube channel with seasonal background music and scenery.

Shea’s never-play list puts her directly at odds with a few other agents: smooth jazz. Shea notes she never plays “anything that sounds like the Weather Channel.”.

In a recent development, marcel Finkelstein of Team BlackStar at eXp Realty hosts open houses every Sunday across Monmouth County, Newly introduced Jersey. He sees music as more of an icebreaker than a staging tool.

His Apple Music rotation includes lounge instrumentals, vocal-free dance-pop and Bon Entendeur. It also has Afro house from DJ Alex Niyazov and the warm trumpet and sax of Fausto Papetti and Paul Mauriat.

He uses the same approach whether the listing is a $600,000 two-bedroom condo in Manalapan or a $2 million six-bedroom in Colts Neck.

“I want the atmosphere to feel calm, comfortable and welcoming, rather than like a sales presentation,” Finkelstein noted.

Finkelstein added that his Instagram followers also know how much he loves music.

Sources indicate that “Every week, I share newly introduced songs and incorporate music into my stories and posts about homes,” he stated. “It’s a personal interest that carries through into how I present properties.”.

Industry observers note that on setup, agents who play music give similar advice. Keep the volume low enough that buyers can ask questions and the agent can hear their feedback. Use one good speaker rather than several.

Industry observers note that bassova puts hers in the middle of the home, and Seeney puts a small Bluetooth speaker in the kitchen. When sellers have a Sonos system, Daniels connects to it from her MacBook or iPad. Otherwise, she brings her own Bose speaker.

It has been revealed that kilmer runs her music from an iPad instead of her phone. “That way, incoming calls and texts don’t interrupt the music,” she remarked.

It has been revealed that as for proof, none of the agents Inman spoke with track music as a performance metric. Bassova remarked she gets buyer feedback that certain homes feel relaxing, but nothing tied to days on market or offers.

It has been revealed that so the evidence is anecdotal, and the playlists don’t agree. Agents can’t even settle on jazz. Both camps share one goal: the buyer should notice the home, not the soundtrack.

As Bassova remarked, “If the buyer begins to think about the music, then it is having a negative impact.”.

Bitcoin (BTC) bull and SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci has argued that the world's biggest cryptocurrency could find a critical bottom as soon as this week.

Scaramucci's comments follow the leading cryptocurrency's struggle to recover from a catastrophic crypto market crash that took BTC to its lowest price level in over two years.

In a recent development, in the latest episode of All Things Markets on Nov. 20, the SkyBridge Capital founder joined Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz to discuss a potential bottom for Bitcoin.

Scaramucci shared his view that Bitcoin could see its bottom on Nov. 25, citing the cryptocurrency's four-year halving cycle as the driving force behind his comments.

"Before we came on, I asked ChatGPT when's the expected halving for Bitcoin," Scaramucci explained.

It has been revealed that "And then when are we 500 days out from that halving? And the estimate was November 25th," he added.

This prediction stems from the idea that Bitcoin's price trends could follow a predictable four-year cycle that coincides with the cryptocurrency's halving events, when the fresh BTC supply is cut in half.

This theory suggests that Bitcoin could find its major bottom around the 500-day mark before its next halving, expected in 2028.

However, these theories are by no means a certainty when it comes to predicting future price action, especially with the current level of institutional participation and macroeconomic forces impacting the crypto market to an unprecedented extent.

During the conversation, Novogratz also took note of Bitcoin's history of forming double bottoms during its four-year cycles.

"And every four years, Bitcoin double bottomed," Novogratz remarked.

At the time, the Galaxy Digital CEO's comments suggested a potentially positive scenario, as Bitcoin had been able to hold its psychological $60,000 price level.

"If it doesn't break 60, that could be a good sign," he noted.

In a recent development, unfortunately for Bitcoin, the cryptocurrency subsequently crashed below this critical price point. This has left some wondering whether the cryptocurrency has already found its ultimate bottom.

During the same conversation, Novogratz suggested that Bitcoin's short-term outlook could largely depend on the current situation in the stock market.

Specifically, the billionaire remarked that a rebound in tech stocks could lead to a strong rally in Bitcoin's price.

According to recent reports, "If we put in a bottom in the next couple days in the S&P here, down 3% from here, down 5% from here. And we have a rally back up. Man, Bitcoin is going to rally hard with it," Novogratz predicted.

However, he also warned that Bitcoin could see a lot of market-driven movements going forward, as opposed to crypto-specific movements.

"I think we're going to be stuck tethered to general sentiment and risk," he said.

Novogratz also believes that Bitcoin could trade in a range between $60,000 and $75,000 before a breakout or breakdown becomes apparent.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin plunged to around $55,100 on Nov. 21, its lowest price level since September 2024, following another severe wave of sell-offs in the crypto market.

According to recent reports, it then bounced back strongly to climb above $60,000 again, albeit briefly, before falling back to around $59,000 on Nov. 22.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:13 EST / NOVEMBER 26 2026.

An investigation has shed light on links between some Nvidia Corp. partners and companies that are based in China or are accused of breaching export controls.

In a recent development, the analysis was carried out by C4ADS, a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit, at the request of CBS News. The outlet published the findings Wednesday evening.

Recent findings suggest that the first focus of the investigation was a San Jose, California-based firm called RiCloud AI Inc. It’s an Nvidia preferred partner, which means that it can buy the chipmaker’s high-end graphics processing units. Companies with that partner destination also have access to Nvidia’s GPU software and technical support services.

Sources indicate that the investigation determined that RiCloud AI is a unit of Shenzen-based Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Ltd. The latter firm’s chief executive reportedly has a degree from a university run by China’s military. Yuxing’s chair, in turn, previously worked at a Chinese tech firm that drew national security scrutiny in Australia.

RiCloud AI recently signed a $120 million deal to lease Nvidia-powered servers to a Taiwanese whiskey company. The latter firm generated just $609,000 in profits last year.

The investigation also looked into a organization called Topmost Corp. It’s reportedly linked to a California businessman who was recently indicted for allegedly smuggling GPUs to China.

According to CBS News, Topmost’s website states that it’s an authorized reseller of Nvidia partner 2CRSi Inc. The latter organization makes servers powered by the chipmaker’s GPUs. Last month, it disclosed that it received a grand jury subpoena in connection with a client “we ourselves had reported to the authorities.”.

The report also noted that California-based Aivres Inc. has exported $3 billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to Southeast Asia since 2024. It’s a subsidiary of Inspur, a Chinese tech firm that is on the U.S. Commerce Department’s Entity List. Organizations on the list are subject to trade restrictions.

Sources indicate that U.S. regulations prohibit companies from exporting Nvidia’s most advanced GPUs to China. Earlier this month, the Commerce Department closed a loophole that Chinese tech firms used to bypass those restrictions. The tech firms in questions rented access to Nvidia GPUs deployed in data centers outside China.

Some of the data centers used by Chinese companies are in Southeast Asia. On Wednesday, the Financial Times reported that Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping GPU-equipped servers to four countries in the region. It’s reportedly unclear whether the move is temporary.

Separately, CNBC reported that companies have put an “unusually high” number of Nvidia GPUs up for sale since the Commerce Department confirmed the new restrictions. It’s believed the chips were intended for data centers that are used by Chinese firms. According to the report, thousands of high-end B300 GPUs are among the processors that were put up for sale.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Minneapolis-based Luminate Bank has agreed to acquire select assets and the mortgage origination operations of Real Genius, expanding the bank’s reach into the digital mortgage channel, the companies announced Wednesday.
  • Industry observers note that online consumer-direct lender Real Genius, which was originally a division of FirstBank, will operate as a division of Luminate Bank and remain as a consumer-facing brand.
  • Nathan Raich, executive vice president of mortgage lending at Luminate Bank, noted the move is aimed at giving borrowers more flexibility in how they work with the institution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Minneapolis-based Luminate Bank has agreed to acquire select assets and the mortgage origination operations of Real Genius, expanding the bank’s reach into the digital mortgage channel, the companies announced Wednesday.

Industry observers note that online consumer-direct lender Real Genius, which was originally a division of FirstBank, will operate as a division of Luminate Bank and remain as a consumer-facing brand. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Nathan Raich, executive vice president of mortgage lending at Luminate Bank, noted the move is aimed at giving borrowers more flexibility in how they work with the institution.

“Some homebuyers want a mortgage professional beside them at every step, while others prefer a more self-directed, digital experience,” Raich remarked in a statement. “Mortgage lending isn’t becoming exclusively digital or exclusively relationship-driven. The opportunity is to be great at both and give customers the freedom to choose.”.

Luminate Bank was formed after a team of mortgage executives acquired the bank in 2020, with a strategy of building a “concierge” financial experience that blends traditional mortgage lending with depository services, co-founder and president of mortgage lending Eric Lovins remarked in a recent interview with HousingWire’s Reverse Mortgage Daily.On the Real Genius deal, Lovins said that Luminate has been working on integration planning and evaluating the organizational structure.

“Our focus is on creating a strong platform for sustainable, profitable growth while ensuring we have the right people, resources and infrastructure to support the business,” he mentioned.

According to recent reports, according to Lovins, Real Genius’s leadership team previously helped build and operate FirstBank’s ConsumerDirect mortgage platform, which delivered more than 50,000 loans over nine years and contributed to a mortgage business that generated approximately $6 billion in annual production. In 2012, the division of FirstBank became Real Genius under the leadership of CEO Jamie Thornton.

“We see tremendous value in that experience and the opportunity to build on it,” Lovins remarked.

He added that the deal leverages Luminate’s broader mortgage and banking platform and represents another notable step in expanding its national mortgage presence. The company’s strategy continues to focus on both organic growth and strategic acquisitions.

It has been revealed that earlier this year, Luminate acquired assets of Illinois-based First State Mortgage Services, extending its footprint across the Midwest and central U.S. Many members of First State Mortgage’s team, led by CEO and president Rene Shaffer, joined Luminate.

It has been revealed that luminate has originated about $3.8 billion year to date, according to mortgage technology platform InGenius. The company had 433 sponsored loan officers as of Wednesday, per the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System.

In December 2022, Luminate Home Loans — a subsidiary of the bank that has operated since 1998 — brought the more than 200-member NEO Home Loans team, previously part of Celebrity Home Loans, onto its platform. This boosted Luminate’s distributed retail presence at a time when many independent mortgage banks were contracting.

In October 2024, however, Luminate revealed that it would shut down the NEO Home Loans division. The manufacturer remarked the decision was driven by a desire to “focus on integrating mortgage lending into its core banking services to better serve clients and build long-term financial relationships.” The NEO group is now partnered with AI-focused mortgage lender Better.com.

Amazon threatens to leave NYC again, this time over delivery bill, as it rallies customers to fight it

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:51 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:51 pm.
  • In a recent development, the Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to New Yorkers’ doors.
  • Industry observers note that the legislation, known as the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would apply to companies that run last-mile delivery facilities in the city.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:51 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:51 pm.

Amazon and Latest York City are fighting again.

In a recent development, the Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to New Yorkers’ doors. It’s also asking its customers to help fight the bill.

Industry observers note that the legislation, known as the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would apply to companies that run last-mile delivery facilities in the city. Amazon is the main target, but FedEx and several regional couriers would also be covered.

Companies would need a license from the city’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, which would also investigate complaints. The bill was introduced in February.

Recent findings suggest that on Thursday, Amazon began showing New York City customers pop-up messages and a homepage banner that reads, “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The notices link to a form and a pre-written letter customers can send to their council members to oppose the bill, Bloomberg reported. Amazon pointed GeekWire to a study by consulting firm AKRF estimating the bill would raise consumer costs by $409 to $664 a year, but didn’t detail how it arrived at the per-order figure.

In a blog post, Amazon said it relies on a network of small delivery businesses in the city. “If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city,” the firm wrote. “That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.”.

It has been revealed that amazon debuted its Delivery Service Partners program in 2018, letting entrepreneurs start their own companies to deliver Amazon packages in Amazon-branded vans and uniforms. The companies hire their own drivers, while Amazon pays them to deliver and offers discounts on vehicles, fuel and insurance. The model lets Amazon expand its delivery network without directly employing drivers.

According to recent reports, in a statement to GeekWire, Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said the bill “as written” would threaten more than 40 small delivery businesses the manufacturer works with in the city and the more than 5,000 New Yorkers they employ. More than 2,000 Amazon employees also work at its delivery facilities in the city, the company said.

“We’re hopeful this bill doesn’t pass as written,” Nantel mentioned. “But so far, key City Council members seem uninterested in learning about our delivery operations.” Amazon said neither Council Member Tiffany Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, nor Mayor Zohran Mamdani has accepted its offer to visit a delivery facility. The manufacturer also said customers sent about 20,000 emails to council members within six hours of the campaign’s launch Thursday morning.

Recent findings suggest that the standoff echoes Amazon’s 2019 reversal on its second headquarters. That February, the manufacturer abruptly canceled plans to build a 25,000-person “HQ2” office in Long Island City, Queens, after more than a year of competition among cities to host it. Amazon blamed “a number of state and local politicians” who opposed the project, which drew fierce criticism over roughly $3 billion in government incentives.

Sources indicate that amazon stuck with its prepares for Arlington, Va., and Nashville and didn’t reopen its search. Polls at the time indicated most Fresh Yorkers supported the deal, but Queens officials, labor leaders and activists fought it. State Sen. Michael Gianaris, who led the opposition, accused Amazon of trying to shake down governments to get its way.

It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise Newly introduced Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections.We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.If… https://t.co/UWXVTJhRL6.

In a recent development, city leaders backing the delivery bill see a familiar pattern. “Amazon is once again making spurious attacks against this commonsense legislation that would make workers and our streets safer,” stated Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, who called Amazon’s warning a “dishonest scare tactic.”.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin questioned Amazon’s cost claims in a post on X.

“It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise New Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections,” she wrote, adding that the council is “crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.”.

Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon’s subcontractor model “leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets,” CNBC reported.

Supporters, including the Teamsters union, which has sought to organize Amazon drivers and warehouse workers, say the bill would make the work safer and make it harder for Amazon to distance itself from driver injuries.

Amazon disputes that the bill would improve safety. The company stated it has invested more than $2.5 billion in driver safety since 2019, that the serious crash rate for its drivers in Latest York City fell 35.7% from 2024 to 2025, and that drivers there have averaged nearly $24 an hour since January 2025, with required health coverage and paid time off.

Meanwhile, business groups have run ads against the bill and warned they may sue the city if it passes, according to CNBC. The measure is awaiting review by Menin.

It has been revealed that XRP Ledger's network activity has dropped sharply, losing around 60% of the consumers it had yesterday. The decline comes amid a serious price correction and increased pressure on the cryptocurrency market. Selling pressure remains high, and the declining number of users is not helping the price.

XRPScan's data demonstrated 250,000 people 24 hours ago, while today's reading shows barely 92,000 users. While the drop is significant, it should not be considered critical on its own. The decline partly reflects a regular weekend slowdown, when traders are generally less active, but it comes alongside the price correction and broader selling pressure.

Sources indicate that the highest point for this metric in November was 300,000, with a monthly average of approximately 200,000 active users. The number of users is a critical metric for the network's health, and a decline toward 100,000 often comes before bullish sentiment among investors. The current drop does not guarantee that sentiment will turn, especially as the price remains under pressure.

Apart from the negative on-chain trend, XRP's price performance has also been weak. The price lost roughly 5% from its November 19 close and even fell below the $0.90 price level, which was expected to serve as a foundation for recovery. XRP was around $0.915 on November 22 after closing at $0.9604 three days earlier.

The trend remains bearish, and the decline could become significantly worse.

In a recent development, few expected a surge in market liquidations so soon, as Bitcoin fell below the $60,000 price level. XRP and other altcoins followed the broader market trend and suffered serious losses.

Interest in the network appears to be weakening as the price correction continues, so this drop in activity is not helping XRP's recovery.

A potential recovery above $0.9 could be the key to a quick rebound. However, the overall trend remains bearish and is unlikely to change unless significant market events occur.

by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 6:33 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 6:33 pm.

Redmond, Wash.-based RBC Signals has confirmed a $10 million strategic growth investment aimed at accelerating the organization’s expansion into government satellite data services and the commercialization of emerging space technologies.

RBC Signals supports satellite operators by arranging access to a global network of ground stations, including its own assets and antenna facilities operated by partners.

Recent findings suggest that in August, for example, Blue Origin and RBC Signals confirmed a partnership to build out the ground infrastructure for Blue Origin’s Quartz communications network. RBC Signals is also a provider for the U.S. Space Force’s Joint Antenna Marketplace.

Sources indicate that the newly revealed investment was led by Washington Harbour Partners, a private investment firm based in Washington, D.C. The firm ranked sixth among all defense technology investors in the Silicon Valley Defense Group’s 2026 NatSec100 Report.

“Our vision has always been to build a global, secure network of networks that makes space connectivity more accessible, flexible and reliable,” Ron Faith, RBC Signals’ president and CEO, stated today in a news release.

In a recent development, “By bringing together infrastructure, partners and emerging technologies, we’re creating a dual-use platform that can evolve alongside the needs of the national defense and the commercial space industry,” Faith noted. “This investment from Washington Harbour Partners will help us accelerate that vision by expanding our government services business and bringing emerging capabilities such as higher frequency bands, optical connectivity, intersatellite links and space domain awareness to market.”.

Sources indicate that mina Faltas, founder and CEO of Washington Harbour Partners, highlighted RBC Signals’ role in addressing the growing demand for space connectivity. “We see tremendous potential in the manufacturer’s ability to deliver mission-critical capabilities, and we’re excited to support the team as they enter this next phase of growth,” Faltas mentioned.

Another XRP Record Ahead? Ripple CEO Predicts XRP Demand Surge as Inflation-Stricken Markets Seek Alternatives to Fiat

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that XRP could be on the verge of another major adoption milestone as inflation-hit economies increasingly look for alternatives to traditional currencies.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Ripple frontman sees growing potential for the cryptocurrency, arguing that demand could rise over time as people in struggling markets seek ways to protect their wealth from weakening fiat currencies.
  • Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes inflation-hit economies could become an increasingly important source of demand for XRP as people seek alternatives to traditional currencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that XRP could be on the verge of another major adoption milestone as inflation-hit economies increasingly look for alternatives to traditional currencies. At least that’s according to Brad Garlinghouse.

Recent findings suggest that the Ripple frontman sees growing potential for the cryptocurrency, arguing that demand could rise over time as people in struggling markets seek ways to protect their wealth from weakening fiat currencies. His comments spotlight a potential new driver of XRP adoption and raise fresh questions about how far demand could grow.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes inflation-hit economies could become an increasingly important source of demand for XRP as people seek alternatives to traditional currencies. Speaking during a recent interview with Bloomberg Television at the Singapore FinTech Festival, he explained how persistent inflation and declining purchasing power could encourage more people to explore digital assets.

“XRP is going to draw people’s interest over time, particularly in markets where you have more inflationary dynamics,” he opined.

Garlinghouse argued that the declining value of fiat currencies could make assets with predictable or limited supplies more attractive to investors. To illustrate his point, he cited the U.S. dollar, describing it as one of the world’s best-managed currencies while noting that it had lost approximately half its value over the past decade.

Industry observers note that he added that the situation is considerably worse in countries with weaker monetary management, where some national currencies have reportedly lost between 80% and 90% of their value. Such conditions, in his view, could strengthen the appeal of digital assets whose supplies cannot be expanded at the discretion of central banks or governments.

Sources indicate that however, scarcity alone is not enough to attract investors. Garlinghouse also highlighted liquidity as an vital consideration, noting that people want assets they can easily hold, transfer, and exchange. This combination could work in XRP’s favor as interest in alternative financial assets grows across inflation-hit markets.

It has been revealed that his remarks point to a potential source of XRP demand beyond speculative trading and institutional investment. While increased interest does not guarantee sustained buying pressure or higher prices, broader adoption in economies struggling with currency depreciation could ultimately boost XRP’s long-term appeal.

During the interview, Amin also asked Garlinghouse whether he could see Bitcoin eventually rocketing to the $1 million mark, a target previously floated by several prominent figures in the crypto industry.

The Ripple chief was receptive to the possibility, although he admitted that predicting when such a milestone might happen was difficult. His optimism was largely rooted in the declining purchasing power of traditional currencies rather than any specific Bitcoin price model.

Bitcoin has a hard supply cap of 21 million coins, while XRP’s total supply was established at 100 billion tokens. Their fixed supply structures distinguish them from government-issued currencies, which can be expanded through monetary policy.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, scarcity does not automatically translate into higher valuations or make either cryptocurrency immune to inflation. Both Bitcoin and XRP remain highly volatile assets whose prices are influenced by market demand and broader economic conditions.

Bitcoin surged above $64,400 as it extended its weekend recovery following Friday’s sharp drop below $56,000, while Ripple’s XRP also staged a rebound, briefly reaching $1.02, per CoinGecko. However, both cryptocurrencies have since surrendered part of those gains. At the time of writing, BTC had pulled back to around $61,271, while XRP had also retreated to $0.9435, reflecting renewed selling pressure after the brief recovery.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A borrower earning nearly $197,000 a year usually doesn’t look like a typical candidate for state housing help.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority introduced a homeownership program this month for first responders and law enforcement officers.
  • Colorado is among a growing list of states offering homebuying assistance to public-service workers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A borrower earning nearly $197,000 a year usually doesn’t look like a typical candidate for state housing help. In Colorado, if that borrower is a firefighter, emergency medical technician or police officer, the person now qualifies.

Recent findings suggest that the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority introduced a homeownership program this month for first responders and law enforcement officers. CHFA Colorado Champions uses a upcoming state law that raises income limits for eligible borrowers.

Colorado is among a growing list of states offering homebuying assistance to public-service workers. The goal is to give them more chances to live near where they serve. Maryland, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Texas, Florida and South Carolina also offer similar programs.

It has been revealed that earlier this month, Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont unveiled a latest homeownership assistance program for first responders. It offers up to $25,000 in forgivable down payment and closing cost assistance. The program stems from a law Lamont signed this year.

“By helping reduce one of the biggest barriers to buying a home, we’re investing in the people who serve our state and the communities that depend on them,” Lamont said in a statement.

CHFA Colorado Champions arrives as the housing market weakens, following several years of zoning and regulatory reform.

Colorado’s single-family housing market has been steadily cooling since spring, according to HousingWire Intelligence data through Nov. 20. Inventory peaked in September and has barely eased, while median list prices have fallen since July. Homes are also taking longer to sell, with days on market rising since late July and price reductions staying elevated.

The latest weekly figures show no reversal, with single-family homes taking a median 91 days to sell, up from 84. The median single-family list price is $599,000, and about 48% of single-family listings carry price cuts, the data show.

It has been revealed that lawmakers have spent years trying to improve affordability, mostly by loosening local land-use rules. In 2024, Gov. Jared Polis signed laws requiring more density near transit and clearing the way for accessory dwelling units. The package also removed some parking minimums for urban multifamily housing and lifted limits on unrelated people living together.

A law Polis signed this year requires towns with more than 2,000 people to allow housing on certain small parcels. Eligible land belongs to school districts, colleges, transit districts, housing authorities and qualifying nonprofits. The law takes effect Dec. 31, 2027, while lot-size bills failed in the Legislature this year.

Senate Bill 26-053, a bipartisan law, raised CHFA’s mortgage income limits to 110% of standard guidelines. That allows eligible borrowers earning up to $196,810 a year to qualify.

It has been revealed that the program offers a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage. The program covers down payment and closing costs up to the lesser of $25,000 or 4% of the first mortgage. Borrowers apply through a CHFA participating lender.

The aid is a second mortgage. Repayment is deferred until the term ends, the first mortgage is paid off, or the borrower sells, refinances or moves.

CHFA Executive Director Thomas Bryan stated in a statement that first responders keep communities safe. Many can’t afford local homes, he added.

“They should be able to live where they serve,” Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer, one of the law’s sponsors, remarked in a statement.

NAR saved for his $541K exit; now it won’t pay, ex-CFO says

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.
  • Recent findings suggest that pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005.
  • Industry observers note that pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005. To avoid booking the full expense when a senior vice president retired, NAR created a Compensation Reserve that let it steadily set aside funds throughout the executive’s tenure, which it would release at retirement. Pierpoint helped establish the reserve in 2005 at the direction of former NAR CEO Dale Stinton, court documents noted.

Industry observers note that pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind. The former CFO said he was key in executing the buyer-broker commission settlement payout, which totaled $418 million. The first settlement payment, totaling roughly $200 million, was issued in February 2025, with subsequent payments of $72 million per year until the full $418 million is paid.

Pierpoint said he notified NAR of his impending retirement in late 2024 and requested his retirement payout. However, six days before his last day with NAR, Pierpoint alleged that a Grant Thornton auditor named White — there is no first name listed in the court documents — emailed him and said that “NAR had been ‘unable to locate any policy or verify any consistent practice’ concerning the Compensation Reserve or ‘the payout to executives of a full year of salary upon retirement.'”.

Sources indicate that white also allegedly remarked that the Compensation Reserve “was not used to fund” the exit packages of eight other senior vice presidents who retired before Pierpoint, which are listed in the court documents as L.J., F.S., B.M., D.H., J.G.,  J.B., D.G. and B.G. Real Estate News said L.J., D.G. and B.G. are likely former general counsel Laurie Janik, former SVP of talent development and resources Donna Gland, and former senior vice president and CEO Bob Goldberg.

As a result, Grant Thornton mentioned it was “unable to approve the payout of a full year’s compensation without any concrete proof that such act is mandated by an employment agreement, policy or strategy.”.

Pierpoint claimed NAR had the funds to pay his retirement benefit and provided a ledger outlining what the Association allegedly reserved from December 2014 to December 2024. He also said the trial balances NAR provided to outside auditors, including Grant Thornton, included evidence of the Compensation Reserve’s existence and purpose.

According to recent reports, “NAR carried its obligation to Pierpoint at approximately 97.6 cents on the dollar three months before it refused to pay him anything,” the complaint read. “The practice NAR now claims it cannot verify is documented in NAR’s own ledger, its own year-end schedules, its own payroll records and its own audit files, and was paid to every one of Pierpoint’s predecessors who retired. NAR did not stop believing in its obligation; it stopped wanting to pay it.”.

Visualized with the help of AI.

Pierpoint’s counsel accused NAR of shirking its obligation to pay the former CFO due to its financial woes after the settlement. In December 2025, former NAR president Kevin Sears remarked the buyer-broker commission settlement saved the Association’s finances — the other option was to file an appeal and declare bankruptcy.

“John Pierpoint helped guide NAR through an extraordinarily challenging period in its history, including the financial consequences of the antitrust litigation,” mentioned David Fish, an attorney with Workplace Law Partners, P.C., who represents Pierpoint. “After nearly four decades of service, he expected the organization to honor the same retirement compensation practice it had followed for other senior executives.”.

“We believe the evidence will establish that the financial pressures following the antitrust verdict did not relieve NAR of its obligation to pay compensation earned by its employees,” he added.

Pierpoint’s counsel is requesting that NAR pay the $541,059 retirement payout, statutory damages of 5 percent of the unpaid amount for each month it remains unpaid, attorneys’ fees and costs, and prejudgment and post-judgment interest. They also seek a jury trial.

NAR denied Pierpoint’s claims, saying that the former CFO has “[mischaracterized] a varied set of individual arrangements with departing executives as a uniform and guaranteed retirement benefit.”.

“Mr. Pierpoint was not entitled to the payment he now seeks, and NAR’s decision was unrelated to its antitrust settlement or its financial condition,” an NAR spokesperson told Inman in an emailed statement. “NAR is committed to appropriate financial controls and responsible stewardship of its members’ dues dollars. NAR pays compensation and benefits that are actually owed, not just because a former executive requests payment. No such obligation exists here, and we intend to vigorously defend against these claims through the appropriate legal process.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 20, 2026 at 7:52 amNovember 20, 2026 at 9:14 am.

It has been revealed that orchard Robotics, an agtech tech giant using artificial intelligence to help growers monitor crops and make farming decisions, has been acquired by John Deere. The deal was revealed Thursday and the terms were not disclosed.

Industry observers note that the startup has developed a system of cameras mounted on tractors and other equipment that gather images as the machines traverse a farm. Orchard’s AI analyzes the images to generate data on vines, trees and crops, which is then used to track growth, yield and health.

“This acquisition connects crop-level intelligence with John Deere technology and equipment that can precisely execute the work in the field,” Tim Marquis, John Deere’s director of farm systems innovation, stated in a statement.

That includes helping farmers target treatments and make better-timed decisions about thinning, spraying and harvesting.

Orchard was founded by CEO Charlie Wu, a Thiel Fellow who dropped out of Cornell University to launch his business in 2022.

“Over these next few years, our goal is to bring the power of Orchard’s industry-leading technology and AI Farming capabilities to every farmer out there,” Wu said in a LinkedIn post. “This is only the beginning of a long and awesome journey ahead.”.

The startup is based in San Francisco and has an office in Seattle. Wu splits his time between the two cities and was a finalist for Young Entrepreneur of the Year at the 2026 GeekWire Awards.

In a recent development, orchard has raised more than $25 million from investors, including a $22 million Series A round announced in September 2025. The startup has 45 employees, according to PitchBook.

According to recent reports, the Pacific Northwest is home to numerous agtech startups. That includes other companies that collect and analyze data, such as Loftus Labs and innov8.ag, as well as IUNU and Koidra, which are focused on greenhouse crops. Businesses tackling field operations include weed destroyers Carbon Robotics and Aigen; rock-removing TerraClear; and irrigation startups FarmHQ and Verdi.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Ethereum developers want to change the gas accounting for validator deposits.
  • The gas calculation already accounts for executing a deposit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum developers want to change the gas accounting for validator deposits. The plan is to measure the request bytes that these deposit events create.

The gas calculation already accounts for executing a deposit. However, after the deposit is finished, a 192-byte request is passed along with the block. Those 192 bytes are excluded from the minimum gas charge, so the same gas limit might allow more data than the initial calculation accounts for.

Under Gloas, there is no fixed cap on the number of deposit requests per block. The execution layer has not capped this either. Gas is the only limiting factor.

Neither EIP-8131 nor EIP-8279 accounts for those request bytes. This means that deposits could become another way to bypass the gas floor once EIP-8279 closes the loophole involving cold storage reads.

In a recent development, A relay contract can call the deposit contract repeatedly, costing around 26,000 gas per deposit. In the author's example, that execution cost is below the point where the gas floor for zero-byte calldata would start to increase the total charge.

This results in a payload of about 1.44 times the block gas limit divided by 64, compared with about 1.15 times the same baseline.

The main issue is the data size, so the proposal directly addresses the data.

It has been revealed that A log from the deposit contract with the deposit event topic counts as 192 bytes before the log entry is added. This is the same condition EIP-6110 uses to turn logs into requests.

The cost of this would be another check that client developers would have to implement and test.

According to recent reports, users are not expected to pay more for regular deposits. The cost of executing a regular deposit is already above the proposed minimum, so the extra 12,288 gas only raises the minimum charge.

The proposal has yet to be scheduled for a network upgrade.
